answer: Agents can earn voting weight by making a time-locked stake that is slashed when independent audits prove their actions were coordinated under fake identities. Splitting one deposit across a hundred accounts does not create more weight, while each account must remain exposed to the same penalty. An attacker must therefore lock substantial capital across a long horizon and risk losing it, not merely generate cheap identities. A cedar-backed audit trail can compare behavior across accounts and flag synchronized transfers; the delta is that Sybil creation becomes costly capital at risk.
